hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 21
hunts.subtitle: Quail opens, the moon is nearly full, and the squirrels will not be consulting the calendar.

rules.title: Today's rules at a glance
items: **Quail opens today**, Nov 21. Regular small game: carry your license, no HIP needed.
**Crow is open today** (Wed, Fri, Sat only). Dove (to Nov 28) and snipe are open. Both need HIP and a plug holding 3 shells total.
**Hunter orange is required.** Deer gun season stays open for other hunters until Jan 1. Bear season ends Nov 22.
Woodcock is NOT open yet (opens Dec 10).
Clocks are on standard time. Next change: Sunday Mar 14, 2027 (spring forward).
rules.note: Confirm seasons and bag limits in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you go.

items: Walk-in (5:55 am): about **44F**, wind **NE 3 mph**, cloudy.
9 am: about **56F**, NE 6 mph. The day warms to about 71F, so cool your game fast.
Wind: **NE 2 to 6 mph** all morning. Gusts were not listed.
Sky: mostly cloudy (64 to 86 percent). Rain chance **3 to 6 percent** this morning.
Sunrise **6:50 am**. Legal light **6:20 am** (sunrise minus 30 minutes).
Moon: **waxing gibbous, about 92 percent**. It sets about 3:22 am, so the walk-in is dark. Full moon is Tuesday.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: a bright moon that set before dawn, mild air and a light breeze mean squirrels and rabbits fed late last night. Expect them to move from first light and again as the air warms after 8:00.
conditions.hours_note: Hourly figures come from a backup weather page, not the National Weather Service table. Gusts were not listed.

in_season.tip: Feed trees with fresh cuttings. Mild, cloudy air keeps them moving.
Thick edges near the feed bins. Solo kick-and-wait push at 7:45.
No covey seen here yet. Bonus only. Listen at first light.
Watch the sky north of you. Sky shots only to the north.
Snipe on the beaver mud. Needs HIP and a 3-shell plug.

in_season: Raccoon and opossum are open. Take only a sure, close shot.
Ducks and rails are open but poor fits for this land. Skip them today.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.
Bear and bobcat are open. You do not hunt them. Stay aware near the swamp.

plan.title: Bin Corner Oak
plan.why: New spot today: the **biggest oak or hickory about 30 paces northwest of the old feed bins, at the loop trail's southeast corner**. Sit against its trunk facing **northwest**. The light northeast breeze crosses from your right, so your scent drifts off behind your left shoulder. The rising sun comes up behind your right shoulder and lights the trunks ahead. Acorn and hull sign under the oak shows squirrels feed here, and the thick edge around the bins holds rabbits. Every shot goes between WNW and NNE with a trunk or the ground behind. The bins and the field are behind you, so never turn toward them with the gun.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail, about 25 minutes before legal light. Red light only. 20 steps, stop 10 seconds. Gun unloaded.
Follow the loop to its southeast corner. Stop 30 paces short of the bins and sit against the big oak, facing NW. Load #4 with the plug in. Red light off.
Legal light. Stay still. Listen for a quail covey call and for gnawing and falling hulls. Scan trunks 20 to 40 yards out, WNW round to NNE.
Sunrise. Watch lit trunks for tail flicks. Run the backstop check on every squirrel before the shot.
Seated hour done. Unload. Start the solo rabbit push along the thick edge north of the bins, heading north. Kick, wait 30 seconds. Shots N, W, or NE only.
Work west along the loop toward the main trail, sunny edges first. Squirrels warm up and move again as the air passes 50F.
Unload. Count shells. Walk out by the main trail, doing the land task.
Unloaded and out. Cool any game right away, since the day heads to 71F. See the skill lesson to clean it.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in). Squirrel and rabbit to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for a close rabbit, a quail flush, or a dove.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**No 00 buckshot carried.**
**Choke: Modified.** Fine for everything today.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on a squirrel only, with a trunk or the ground certain behind it.
Pack - GRAB: gun, phone, water bottle filled, tell someone your plan and return time.
Pack - CHARGE: headlamp and spare flashlight before bed.
Pack - RESTOCK after the hunt: water, coffee or tea, nibble, nitrile gloves, .22 LR count, fatwood.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
Swap shells in the open with the muzzle north. Count every shell in and out.
The bins and the field are SE and behind your seat. Never swing the muzzle past north-east.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game here. Grays work oaks, hickories, and hollies. A fox squirrel may show in the pines.
Cloudy, mild air after a bright moon: expect movement from first light, then another burst after 8:00.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards, head and neck on a trunk squirrel.
With the .22: head only, wood or ground behind.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Line up the fall with two trees so you can find it.

details.title: Technique: sit the oak
steps: Look under the oak for split hulls and bright cut nuts. Fresh pieces are pale inside.
Sit still 20 minutes. Squirrels return once the woods go quiet.
Listen for gnawing, then look up the trunk toward the sound.

after: Tip: if a squirrel flattens on a limb, it has seen you. Freeze and wait. It will move again.
Tip: shoot the one on the trunk with wood behind it, not the one against open sky.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails hold in the thick tangle around the feed bins and the loop edges. They sit tight until you are close.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards, head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: kick and wait
steps: Take 3 steps, kick a thick clump, step back, and stand still 30 seconds.
A running rabbit often stops once to look back.
Find the black eye and ear line, then check the backstop and shoot.

after: Tip: walk the edge so the cover is on your N or W side, never your south.

animals.name: Quail (opens today)
paragraphs: Northern bobwhite. No covey has been seen here, so this is a bonus, not the plan.
If one exists it holds in thick low cover beside open ground and flushes all at once.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 in the right pocket is the quail load. #4 works to 30 yards.
Pick ONE bird. Never shoot into the brown of the covey.
Shoot only birds flying N, W, or E. Let south-bound birds go.

details.title: Technique: listen first
steps: At legal light, stay still and listen for the whistled covey call.
If you hear it, mark the direction. Move 3 steps, then stop.
On the flush, swing through one bird and follow through.

after: Tip: a covey flushes wild if you stride up. Stop short and let it settle.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows cross the pine tops and swamp in the morning. Saturday is an open day.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 25 to 35 yards on an incoming bird.
Shoot only when the sky north of you is clear.

after: Tip: hard cawing and circling means crows are mobbing a hawk or owl. Look up there.

animals.name: Dove and snipe (opportunity)
paragraphs: Doves may cross the wood line. Snipe use the wet mud by the beaver lodge. Both need HIP and a 3-shell plug.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 20 to 30 yards.
Shoot only birds flying N, W, or E with a clear sky behind.

after: Tip: a snipe flushes with a scratchy call and zig-zags. Wait for it to straighten.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both feed at night near the swamp and the bins. At first light the last ones head to hollow trees.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind and touch the eye with a stick. Opossums play dead.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: hair snagged on the bin edges means one passed close.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season is open through Nov 22, so you may hear other hunters. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Skinning and quartering squirrel and rabbit
skill.principle: Warm days spoil meat fast. Clean the animal within the hour, keep hair off the meat, and get it cold.

sections.title: Squirrel: cut and pull
steps: Wear nitrile gloves. Lay the squirrel on its belly.
Lift the skin at the middle of the back and cut a small slit across it.
Put two fingers into the slit, one each way, and pull the skin apart toward head and tail.
Cut off the head, tail, and all four feet.
Slit the belly, remove the insides, and rinse in cold water.

sections.title: Rabbit: peel
steps: Gloves on. Cut off the feet and head.
Pinch the skin at the belly, slit it, and peel it off toward the head and tail like a sock.
Open the belly and remove the insides.
Check the liver. Discard the rabbit if it has white spots.
Rinse and cool at once.

sections.title: Quarter and cool
steps: Cut off the front legs, then the hind legs at the hip joint.
Cut the saddle (back) away from the rib cage.
Put the pieces in a cooler on ice or in the refrigerator within the hour.
Bury scraps well away from the trails.

details.title: Why the liver check
paragraphs: Rabbits can carry tularemia. White or yellow spots on the liver are the warning. Gloves and a hot cook (well done) protect you.

skill.checkpoint: After you clean your first animal, send a note: with what you found and what was hard.

land.intro: Learn which trees feed the squirrels near the bins.
steps: On the walk out, look under the big oak and nearby hickories for split hulls, bright cut nuts, and fresh bark scars.
Count the leaf nests (round clumps of leaves) in the trees around the bins.
Pace from the Junction to the best feed tree.
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: 12 fresh hulls under the oak, 3 leaf nests, 140 paces from the Junction.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between WNW and NNE, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal. Sky shots at crow, dove, or quail only to the north.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season and bear season are open for other hunters.
Your seat sits NW of the bins. The bins and the field are behind you. Keep the muzzle north when you stand.
Unload before crossing logs, the swamp edge, or open ground.
Mornings start near 44F and reach the mid 50s by 9. Wear layers you can open. Cool meat quickly on a 71F afternoon.
hunts.regs: Check seasons, bag limits, and migratory bird rules in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you hunt.
hunts.gaps: The National Weather Service hourly page was stale (October data), so the hourly chart comes from a backup weather page. Gusts and the NWS issue time were not available. One earlier source listed a different daily low, so walk-in temperature may be a few degrees off. Moonrise and moonset times were taken from the sun table and assumed to be local time. Rain tomorrow (Sunday) was carried from an earlier check and not re-confirmed. Dove, snipe, rail, duck, and woodcock dates come from the 2026-27 proclamation. Crow dates and bag limits were carried from earlier checks.
